after: ## Two methods that make an idea visible
alt: Two panels. Definition answers “What is it, exactly?” with a dashed boundary separating what counts from what does not. Description answers “What is it like?” with sight, sound, smell, touch and taste radiating from the thing described.
caption: Definition draws boundaries; description makes features vivid.

alt: A formal definition of drought split into term, class (a period of weather) and what distinguishes it (rainfall so far below normal that supplies fall short). Below, five tools for extended definitions with the lesson’s examples: examples, negation, comparison, features and requirements, and the origin of the word.
caption: Formal definitions are compact; extended ones add examples, negation and comparison.

alt: Defining success as a high salary decides the argument about whether college is worthwhile before it starts. Ambrose Bierce’s satirical definition, “Positive, adj. Mistaken at the top of one’s voice”, carries a claim that loudness is not knowledge. Writers should state defensible definitions; readers should test them.
caption: Ask whether a definition is fair, or whether it carries the claim by itself.

alt: Dickens’s fog passage split into labelled parts: the stark opening “Fog everywhere”, the parallel “Fog up the river... fog down the river”, the shift from “flows” among green meadows to “rolls defiled” among pollution, and the whispered judgement “(and dirty)”. A river schematic shows the clean upstream and polluted downstream.
caption: Parallel clauses and a changing verb make the fog inescapable and dirty.

alt: Two weak-to-strong pairs. “Loyalty means being faithful” becomes laughing through a friend’s third retelling of a story. “The market was busy” becomes crates scraping on stone, a vendor shouting the price of figs, and the smell of fish and wet cardboard.
caption: The strong versions do not just assert; they let the reader see an instance.

after: ## Worked example 1: writing an extended definition for an argument
alt: Five steps to a fair definition of cheating: a formal definition (gaining an advantage by methods the rules forbid), noticing that it depends on the rules, extending it with the contrast between copying and an allowed formula sheet, linking it to the claim that the cure is a better question, and checking that it is fair.
caption: A good definition sets fair terms for the argument rather than winning it in advance.
